# Prediction model for length of stay

## Aim and approach

We develop a clinical prediction model for rehabilitation length of stay (`los_bal`, days). The steps are:

1. Prepare the data, recode invalid diagnostic categories as missing, collapse rare diagnostic categories and describe missingness.
2. Handle missing data with multiple imputation (`mice`).
3. Choose a modelling strategy: a negative binomial model with LASSO penalisation.
4. Fit the final model on the full data.
5. Estimate optimism-corrected performance (R², calibration slope) by bootstrapping, **repeating the entire model-building process (imputation, estimation of theta and tuning of the LASSO penalty) in every bootstrap sample**.
6. Assess calibration.

`glmnet` has no built-in negative binomial family, so we use `glmnet` with `family = MASS::negative.binomial(theta)`, where the dispersion parameter `theta` is estimated from the training data each time the model is fitted.

## Step 1: Data preparation

```{r prep}
library(MASS, exclude = "select")
library(mice)

min_n <- 10  # minimum patients for a diagnostic category to stay separate

predictors <- c("age", "sex", "carer_stress", "dementia", "malnutrition",
                "cci", "fracture", "los_pre", "eccs_pre",
                "pm_diag_cat_pre", "twoassist")

dat <- data_import |>
  dplyr::select(los_bal, all_of(predictors)) |>
  mutate(
    across(c(sex, carer_stress, dementia, malnutrition, fracture, twoassist),
           as.integer),
    # Blank entries and the code '8' are not valid categories: treat as missing
    pm_diag_cat_pre = if_else(pm_diag_cat_pre %in% c("", "8"),
                              NA_character_, pm_diag_cat_pre)
  )

n_obs <- nrow(dat)
```

### Invalid diagnostic categories recoded as missing

Blank entries and the value `8` of `pm_diag_cat_pre` are not valid diagnostic categories, so they are recoded to missing (`NA`) in `dat` and will be multiply imputed. This affects `r sum(is.na(dat$pm_diag_cat_pre))` patients (`r sum(data_import$pm_diag_cat_pre == "")` blank, `r sum(data_import$pm_diag_cat_pre == "8")` with the value `8`).

### Collapsing rare diagnostic categories

Diagnostic category has many levels, several with very few patients. Such categories cannot be estimated reliably, and in bootstrap samples they are often absent altogether. Using the patients with an observed category, we collapse every category with **fewer than `r min_n` patients** into a single category, "Other". Collapsing uses only the predictor, not the outcome. Patients with a missing category stay missing.

```{r collapse}
diag_counts <- dat |>
  filter(!is.na(pm_diag_cat_pre)) |>
  count(pm_diag_cat_pre, name = "n") |>
  mutate(Decision = if_else(n < min_n, "Collapsed to 'Other'", "Kept"))

kable(diag_counts, col.names = c("Diagnostic category", "Patients", "Decision"))

collapsed_cats <- diag_counts |> filter(n < min_n) |> pull(pm_diag_cat_pre)
kept_cats      <- diag_counts |> filter(n >= min_n) |> pull(pm_diag_cat_pre)

dat <- dat |>
  mutate(pm_diag_cat_pre = factor(
    if_else(pm_diag_cat_pre %in% collapsed_cats, "Other", pm_diag_cat_pre),
    levels = c(kept_cats, "Other")))
```

The categories collapsed into "Other" are: **`r paste(collapsed_cats, collapse = ", ")`** (`r sum(diag_counts$n[diag_counts$Decision != "Kept"])` patients in total). The categories kept as separate levels are: `r paste(kept_cats, collapse = ", ")`.

```{r diag-after}
kable(count(dat, pm_diag_cat_pre), col.names = c("Category after recoding and collapsing", "Patients"))
```

### Missing data and outcome distribution

```{r missing}
colSums(is.na(dat)) |>
  enframe(name = "Variable", value = "Missing") |>
  filter(Missing > 0) |>
  kable()
```

```{r outcome-dist}
ggplot(dat, aes(los_bal)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5) +
  labs(x = "Length of stay (days)", y = "Patients")

c(mean = mean(dat$los_bal), variance = var(dat$los_bal))
```

A variance well above the mean indicates overdispersion, supporting a negative binomial rather than a Poisson model.

## Step 2: Multiple imputation

Missing values (`eccs_pre` and `pm_diag_cat_pre`) are imputed with `mice`. `eccs_pre` is imputed using predictive mean matching (PMM). `pm_diag_cat_pre` is an unordered categorical variable, and `mice`'s PMM works only with numeric variables, so it is imputed with the `mice` method for nominal factors, polytomous logistic regression (`polyreg`). The imputation model includes all predictors and the outcome (log-transformed, since LOS is skewed).

Because the imputation is part of the model-building process, it is repeated in every bootstrap sample. To combine imputations with a single LASSO fit, we use the **stacked imputed datasets** approach: the $m$ completed datasets are stacked, each row is given weight $1/m$, and cross-validation folds keep all copies of the same patient together. Predictions for a patient are averaged across the $m$ imputed datasets.

```{r impute-fn}
impute_data <- function(d, m, maxit = 10, seed = NA) {
  d$log_los <- log(d$los_bal)
  all_levels <- levels(d$pm_diag_cat_pre)
  # Drop levels absent from this (bootstrap) sample so the imputation model is estimable
  d$pm_diag_cat_pre <- droplevels(d$pm_diag_cat_pre)
  imp_in <- d[, c("log_los", predictors)]

  meth <- make.method(imp_in)
  meth["log_los"] <- ""
  meth["eccs_pre"] <- "pmm"
  meth["pm_diag_cat_pre"] <- "polyreg"
  pred <- make.predictorMatrix(imp_in)

  imp <- mice(imp_in, m = m, maxit = maxit, method = meth,
              predictorMatrix = pred, printFlag = FALSE, seed = seed)

  map(seq_len(m), \(k) {
    out <- complete(imp, k)
    out$pm_diag_cat_pre <- factor(as.character(out$pm_diag_cat_pre), levels = all_levels)
    out$los_bal <- d$los_bal
    out$log_los <- NULL
    out
  })
}
```

```{r impute-original}
m_final <- 10
imps_full <- impute_data(dat, m = m_final, seed = 2863)
```

## Step 3: Model-fitting functions

Everything that uses the outcome (theta estimation and choice of lambda) is wrapped in one function so it can be repeated in each bootstrap sample. `glmnet` standardises predictors internally and returns coefficients on the original scale. Diagnostic category is one-hot encoded (one column per category, no reference level; the LASSO penalty handles the redundancy), and all columns are penalised.

```{r functions}
make_x <- function(d) {
  model.matrix(
    ~ ., data = d[, predictors],
    contrasts.arg = list(pm_diag_cat_pre = contrasts(d$pm_diag_cat_pre, contrasts = FALSE))
  )[, -1, drop = FALSE]
}

# imps: list of m completed datasets (same patients, same row order)
fit_nb_lasso <- function(imps, nfolds = 10) {
  m <- length(imps)
  n <- nrow(imps[[1]])
  x <- do.call(rbind, map(imps, make_x))
  y <- unlist(map(imps, "los_bal"))
  w <- rep(1 / m, length(y))
  patient <- rep(seq_len(n), times = m)

  # Theta: average of unpenalised NB estimates across imputed datasets
  thetas <- map_dbl(imps, \(d) {
    xd <- make_x(d)
    tryCatch(suppressWarnings(MASS::glm.nb(d$los_bal ~ xd)$theta),
             error = function(e) NA_real_)
  })
  theta <- min(mean(thetas, na.rm = TRUE), 1e4)
  if (!is.finite(theta)) theta <- 10

  # Folds assigned by patient so copies of a patient are never split
  foldid_pat <- sample(rep(seq_len(nfolds), length.out = n))
  foldid <- foldid_pat[patient]

  cv <- cv.glmnet(x, y, weights = w, family = MASS::negative.binomial(theta),
                  alpha = 1, foldid = foldid, type.measure = "deviance")
  list(cv = cv, theta = theta)
}

# Average prediction across the imputed versions of the evaluation data
predict_nb_lasso <- function(fit, imps, type = c("response", "link")) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  preds <- map(imps, \(d) as.numeric(
    predict(fit$cv, newx = make_x(d), s = "lambda.min", type = type)))
  Reduce(`+`, preds) / length(preds)
}
```

## Step 4: Performance measures

We report five measures, all optimism-corrected by the bootstrap. Together they cover explained variation, calibration, prediction error and discrimination.

| Measure | What it tells us | Ideal value |
|---|---|---|
| Deviance-based pseudo-R² | Proportion of negative binomial deviance explained relative to an intercept-only model: $$1 - D_{model}/D_{null}$$ | Higher is better (can be negative in new data) |
| Calibration slope | Slope from regressing observed LOS on the model's linear predictor (negative binomial, fixed theta). Below 1 indicates overfitting | 1 |
| Calibration-in-the-large | Intercept (log scale) of a model with the linear predictor as an offset. Positive means the model under-predicts LOS on average; negative means over-prediction | 0 |
| MAE (days) | Mean absolute error between observed LOS and predicted mean LOS | Lower is better |
| C-index | Probability that, for a randomly chosen pair of patients with different LOS, the patient predicted to stay longer did stay longer (Harrell's C) | 1 (0.5 = no discrimination) |

As a reference, the MAE of a null model that predicts the overall mean LOS for everyone is also reported.

```{r metrics}
perf <- function(fit, imps) {
  y     <- imps[[1]]$los_bal
  theta <- fit$theta
  fam   <- MASS::negative.binomial(theta)
  mu    <- predict_nb_lasso(fit, imps, "response")
  lp    <- predict_nb_lasso(fit, imps, "link")

  dev_model <- sum(fam$dev.resids(y, mu, 1))
  dev_null  <- sum(fam$dev.resids(y, rep(mean(y), length(y)), 1))

  slope <- tryCatch(
    unname(coef(suppressWarnings(glm(y ~ lp, family = fam)))["lp"]),
    error = function(e) NA_real_)
  citl <- tryCatch(
    unname(coef(suppressWarnings(glm(y ~ 1 + offset(lp), family = fam)))[1]),
    error = function(e) NA_real_)

  c(pseudo_r2 = 1 - dev_model / dev_null,
    cal_slope = slope,
    citl      = citl,
    mae       = mean(abs(y - mu)),
    c_index   = unname(Hmisc::rcorr.cens(mu, y)["C Index"]))
}

null_mae <- function(imps) {
  y <- imps[[1]]$los_bal
  mean(abs(y - mean(y)))
}

metric_labels <- c(pseudo_r2 = "Pseudo-R² (deviance)",
                   cal_slope = "Calibration slope",
                   citl      = "Calibration-in-the-large",
                   mae       = "MAE (days)",
                   c_index   = "C-index")
```

## Step 5: Final model on the full data

```{r final-fit}
set.seed(4817)
final_fit <- fit_nb_lasso(imps_full)
apparent <- perf(final_fit, imps_full)

list(theta = final_fit$theta,
     lambda_min = final_fit$cv$lambda.min,
     apparent = round(apparent, 3),
     null_mae = null_mae(imps_full))
```

```{r cv-plot}
plot(final_fit$cv)
```

### Coefficients

Coefficients are on the log scale; exponentiated values are ratios of expected LOS. Variables shrunk exactly to zero are dropped by the LASSO.

```{r coefs}
cf <- coef(final_fit$cv, s = "lambda.min")

tibble(Predictor = rownames(cf), Coefficient = as.numeric(cf)) |>
  mutate(`Ratio of mean LOS` = exp(Coefficient),
         Retained = Coefficient != 0 | Predictor == "(Intercept)") |>
  kable(digits = 3)
```

## Step 6: Bootstrap optimism correction

For each of $B$ bootstrap samples we:

1. Draw a sample of patients with replacement from the original data (with missing values still missing).
2. Impute the bootstrap sample with `mice` ($m = 5$) and refit the **whole** procedure (theta, cross-validated LASSO).
3. Compute performance in the imputed bootstrap sample (apparent) and in the original data (test, using the imputed versions of the original data from Step 2).
4. Optimism = apparent minus test performance.

In the same loop we also refit the model **using only the terms retained in the final model, at the final model's lambda**, and store the coefficients (`boot_coefs`). These are used in Step 8 to give a bootstrap confidence interval for the predicted mean LOS in the calculator. The interval is *conditional* on the selected predictors and penalty (it reflects sampling and imputation variability but not uncertainty about which variables are selected), which is what allows the calculator to ask only for the retained predictors.

The mean optimism is subtracted from the apparent performance of the final model (Harrell's method). This step is computationally intensive (imputation plus cross-validation in every sample).

```{r bootstrap}
B <- 500
m_boot <- 5
set.seed(7352)

# Final-model terms and penalty, used for the conditional CI for the calculator
cf_final <- coef(final_fit$cv, s = "lambda.min")
sel_cols <- setdiff(rownames(cf_final)[as.numeric(cf_final) != 0], "(Intercept)")
lambda_final <- final_fit$cv$lambda.min

# Refit at the final lambda using only the final-model terms
fit_fixed <- function(imps, theta) {
  m <- length(imps)
  x <- do.call(rbind, map(imps, make_x))[, sel_cols, drop = FALSE]
  y <- unlist(map(imps, "los_bal"))
  fit <- glmnet(x, y, weights = rep(1 / m, length(y)),
                family = MASS::negative.binomial(theta), alpha = 1,
                lambda = lambda_final)
  c("(Intercept)" = as.numeric(fit$a0), setNames(as.numeric(fit$beta), sel_cols))
}

boot_out <- map(seq_len(B), \(b) {
  idx <- sample(n_obs, replace = TRUE)
  d_boot <- dat[idx, ]
  tryCatch({
    imps_b <- impute_data(d_boot, m = m_boot)
    fit_b  <- fit_nb_lasso(imps_b)
    app    <- perf(fit_b, imps_b)
    test   <- perf(fit_b, imps_full)
    list(res = tibble(b = b, metric = names(app), apparent = app, test = test,
                      n_nonzero = sum(coef(fit_b$cv, s = "lambda.min")[-1] != 0)),
         coefs = fit_fixed(imps_b, fit_b$theta))
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
}) |>
  compact()

boot_res <- map(boot_out, "res") |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(optimism = apparent - test)

# One row per bootstrap sample: coefficients of the final-model terms
boot_coefs <- do.call(rbind, map(boot_out, "coefs"))

n_boot_ok <- n_distinct(boot_res$b)
n_boot_ok
```

`r n_boot_ok` of `r B` bootstrap samples completed successfully.

```{r boot-summary}
perf_table <- boot_res |>
  group_by(metric) |>
  summarise(Optimism = mean(optimism, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_valid = sum(!is.na(optimism)), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Apparent = apparent[metric],
         `Optimism-corrected` = Apparent - Optimism,
         Measure = metric_labels[metric]) |>
  arrange(match(metric, names(metric_labels)))

perf_table |>
  dplyr::select(Measure, Apparent, Optimism, `Optimism-corrected`) |>
  kable(digits = 3)
```

For reference, the MAE of the null (mean-only) model is `r round(null_mae(imps_full), 1)` days, compared with an optimism-corrected model MAE of `r round(perf_table[perf_table$metric == "mae", "Optimism-corrected"][[1]], 1)` days.

```{r boot-plot}
boot_res |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric_labels[metric], levels = metric_labels)) |>
  ggplot(aes(optimism)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Optimism (apparent minus test)", y = "Bootstrap samples")
```

## Step 7: Calibration

The plot compares predicted with observed LOS, using predictions averaged across the imputed datasets. It is apparent (not optimism-corrected).

```{r calibration}
dat$pred <- predict_nb_lasso(final_fit, imps_full)

ggplot(dat, aes(pred, los_bal)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE) +
  labs(x = "Predicted LOS (days)", y = "Observed LOS (days)")
```

```{r calibration-deciles}
dat |>
  mutate(decile = ntile(pred, 10)) |>
  group_by(decile) |>
  summarise(Predicted = mean(pred), Observed = mean(los_bal), .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(digits = 1)
```

## Step 8: Export the model for the Shiny calculator

The final model is a log-linear model, so the predicted mean LOS for a new patient is

$$\hat\mu = \exp\left(\beta_0 + \sum_j \beta_j x_j\right)$$

using the coefficients on the original (unstandardised) scale from the final LASSO fit. The calculator needs the intercept, the non-zero coefficients, theta, and the observed range of each predictor in the development data (used to flag out-of-bounds inputs). The bootstrap coefficient sets (`boot_coefs`, from Step 6) are also saved, so the calculator can show a 90% bootstrap percentile confidence interval for the predicted mean: the predicted mean is computed under each bootstrap model, and the 5th and 95th percentiles are reported. Everything is saved to `los_app/model.rds`, which is deployed with the app in `los_app/app.R`.

```{r export-model}
cf <- coef(final_fit$cv, s = "lambda.min")
beta <- setNames(as.numeric(cf), rownames(cf))
beta_nz <- beta[beta != 0 & names(beta) != "(Intercept)"]

var_labels <- c(age = "Age (years)", sex = "Sex", carer_stress = "Carer stress",
                dementia = "Dementia", malnutrition = "Malnutrition",
                cci = "Charlson comorbidity index (excluding age)",
                fracture = "Fracture", los_pre = "Preceding hospital LOS (days)",
                eccs_pre = "Preceding hospital ECCS",
                pm_diag_cat_pre = "Diagnostic category (preceding hospital)",
                twoassist = "Two-person assist on admission")

# Predictors with at least one non-zero coefficient (factor dummies start with the variable name)
selected <- predictors[sapply(predictors, \(v) any(startsWith(names(beta_nz), v)))]

var_spec <- map(selected, \(v) {
  x <- dat[[v]]
  if (is.factor(x)) {
    list(var = v, label = var_labels[[v]], type = "factor", levels = levels(x),
         collapsed = collapsed_cats)
  } else if (all(na.omit(x) %in% c(0, 1))) {
    list(var = v, label = var_labels[[v]], type = "binary")
  } else {
    list(var = v, label = var_labels[[v]], type = "numeric",
         min = min(x, na.rm = TRUE), max = max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         p025 = unname(quantile(x, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)),
         p975 = unname(quantile(x, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)),
         median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  }
}) |>
  setNames(selected)

model_export <- list(
  intercept = beta[["(Intercept)"]],
  coefs = beta_nz,
  theta = final_fit$theta,
  var_spec = var_spec,
  boot_coefs = boot_coefs,
  n_dev = n_obs,
  perf = perf_table |> dplyr::select(Measure, Apparent, `Optimism-corrected`)
)

dir.create(paste0(export_path_mac, "los_app"), showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(model_export, paste0(export_path_mac, "los_app/model.rds"))

tibble(Term = names(beta_nz), Coefficient = beta_nz) |> kable(digits = 4)
```

Predictors retained by the LASSO (and therefore requested by the calculator): `r paste(var_labels[selected], collapse = "; ")`.
